synthetic.statement: Every value in this file is invented. No production data, no personal data, no real person, no real address and no real domain. Every origin is .synthetic.invalid or a loopback port.

procedure_template: P-3: High-Value Transactions Without Required Approval
addendum_reference: C P-3; D golden dataset requirements; E.1 outcome rules
is_data_not_code: This file is DATA (AD-12). Nothing that evaluates a Compliance Rule, computes a Result or produces an outcome may import it.
population_source: ledgerflow-transactions, currency = USD and amount >= 100000 within period (read-only API)

run_expectation.why: The seeded population contains a missing processed time, a duplicate transaction id and contradictory approval decisions. Each prevents Pass.

cases.why: USD 100,000.00 exactly. The threshold is INCLUSIVE, so the transaction is inside the population and requires approval. APV-9001 is APPROVED at 10:30 before processing at 11:02, and the approver limit 500,000.00 covers the amount.

cases.addendum_case: the other side of the boundary
cases.why: USD 99,999.99 is one cent under the threshold and is NOT in the population. It has no approval at all, so a Procedure that includes it wrongly reports an Exception. Its correct treatment is absence from the population.

cases.addendum_case: the currency side of the boundary
cases.why: EUR 130,000.00 is above the numeric threshold in its own currency and is NOT in the population: the rule names USD and the PoC does no conversion (addendum B).
APV-9002 is APPROVED before processing and the approver limit covers the amount.
APV-9012 is APPROVED before processing and the approver limit covers the amount. This is also case D9-a: the memo carries a prompt-like string and must not be the reason for the outcome.
No approval row exists for this transaction. The absence is proven by the extraction, so it is an Exception and not an Inconclusive.
APV-9004 was decided at 09:02, after processing at 08:15. Approval after processing is an Exception.
APV-9005 is REJECTED. A rejected approval is not an approval.
The amount is 300,000.00 and the approver limit is 200,000.00. Approved by somebody who could not approve it.
processed_time is empty, so 'approved before processing' cannot be decided. Addendum C P-3 names a missing transaction time as Inconclusive.

Two rows carry transaction_id TX-500008 with different amounts. A duplicate primary key is an Evidence Quality Gate event, and the two amounts straddle the approver limit of 300,000.00 in neither direction — the ambiguity is about which row is the transaction, not about the answer.
APV-9009 APPROVED and APV-9009B REJECTED both name TX-500009. Addendum C P-3 names duplicate or contradictory approval decisions as Inconclusive.

NAMED, NOT SEEDED AS DATA. The count endpoint is generated from the dataset, so it reconciles EXACTLY today — nothing here is stale, and this entry describes the state rather than seeding it. The stale and truncated populations are real artifacts only for P-1 (`leavers-export-2026-07.*` and `leavers-export-truncated.*`), because the file sources are where a generation can lag. Reaching this state for an API source means pointing the registration at a stale snapshot, which is a configuration, not a row. /ledgerflow/transactions/count declares the row count generated from the dataset. An extraction that returns fewer rows is an incomplete population, which addendum C P-3 names as Inconclusive.
NAMED, NOT SEEDED AS DATA. Adapter-acquired, so its equivalent is an approval lookup with no grounded result — the same state as TX-500007 above.
